chapter: Listening to the Troy Floyd records
title: Shadowland Blues, Dixon, and Texas blues singers and TOBA
summary: On Shadowland Blues, Albert describes the quick same-day recording, Dixon's playing, and traveling blues shows such as Ma Rainey and Bessie Smith at Ella B. Moore's Theater in Dallas, the one TOBA house nearby.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, let's see. This is Shadowland Blues.
That's Psychey Collins on his soprano.
This is a different day, as I remember. Same day. Oh, it was made the same day. Same day.

The recording companies in those days didn't have too much time to spend with you. Time was in between the solo. Charlie Dixon off the tubo on the trombone. The seventh That's real blues. Yeah. That guy's got a tremendous feeling. Well, he played with all the great blues singers of those days and times. And a lot of times he played with trombone, a lot of times he played with turbo.
Do you know if he traveled with any of those blues singers?
I saw it. He just played in... Just confined himself to Texas travel. East Texas, West Texas, and Central Texas.
Did you see many of the traveling shows with blues singers there? Not too many. Not too many. Did you ever see Ma Rain? Who is that?

Ma Rainey or Betsy Smith. Yes, yes. They would come through. Well, one of the big outlets for those people were the Ella B. Moore's Theater in Dallas. It was on Central Track. That was one of the few TOBA fields in the South. Oh, I see. Now, this is Keller Jefferson. He died real young.
San Antonio didn't have a TOBA. I think the only one there on that circuit was Ella B. Moore in Dallas. And Ella B. Moore...
Somebody's behind him there on a reed. You can just barely hear him. You'll hear him in a minute. Well, let's stop now. I think it was this.

Yeah, that's Psyche on the soprano. Yeah, yeah. That's the only one that was behind. On this was Psyche. The rhythm section. And Charlie Dixon. That was all behind the scene. Possibly the brass section might have been holding a whole chord or something. A blues chord. Way in the background.
